Put functional direction (tempo, dynamics, vocal style, mood, energy) inside section tags — Suno interprets it. Narrative labels like [VERSE 1 — THE ROOM] carry no generation signal and may be sung.

Creates a genuine tension/lift build before the chorus — Suno adds percussion, harmony layers, and vocal intensity. Keep short, 2-4 lines; without the tag, transitional lyrics may be sung awkwardly as an extra verse line.
Creates an extension or cooldown after the chorus (repeated chant, vocal chops, instrumental hook, or response line). Very effective in pop/EDM; may blend with the chorus in rock/metal.
Something NEW: new chords, melody, potentially a different key; repositions the song's narrative and emotional angle. Distinct from [Breakdown] (something LESS).

Something LESS: subtractive arrangement that strips instruments (typically drums and/or bass) while spotlighting vocals or a single motif; in metal/metalcore it forces a tempo drop and heavy rhythm. Maximum contrast before a high-energy section.
Sudden energy release section (EDM/electronic), typically 10-20 sec.
Hard stop; the most reliable single ending tag, though it may still produce 5-15 seconds of trailing instrumental.
Brief moment of silence.
Building volume/intensity; also a Suno glossary dynamics term — the guide's worked move is 'crescendo into an anthemic chorus'.
Gradual volume decrease at the end.
Short catchy phrase or repeated motif, distinct from a full chorus.

Transitional palette cleanser between major sections; defaults to instrumental and neutralizes energy rather than dramatically shifting it. Chaining [Interlude] with [Solo] is effective for changing movement or tone.
